ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Ronald Reagan

code.originalText: Neurology consultation for Alzheimer's disease staging, medication review, and evening restlessness

text.paragraph: Two-week post-fracture check, with neurology consultation for dementia staging and evening restlessness. [S]

Mr. Reagan is a 90-year-old man with moderate Alzheimer's disease who returns two weeks after his first visit following repair of a right hip fracture, and is seen by neurology on the same day. Oxycodone and diphenhydramine were stopped two weeks ago. His hip aches a little when he walks, and scheduled acetaminophen keeps him comfortable. His caregivers report that he sleeps as well as before without the diphenhydramine and has been no more confused. He finished 35 days of enoxaparin last week, without bruising or bleeding. Home physical therapy continues, and he walks short distances in the house with a front-wheeled walker and standby help. He has had no falls. Grab bars, a raised toilet seat, and night lights went in after the home safety assessment, and loose rugs were taken up. Mild evening restlessness and repeated questions continue; a quiet, unhurried evening routine settles them. He takes donepezil each morning and vitamin D daily from a weekly organizer. [S]

Dementia due to Alzheimer's disease, moderate (FAST stage 5) (F02.B0). Neurology confirms moderate Alzheimer's disease at FAST stage 5, in keeping with the MoCA of 11 two weeks ago. The evening restlessness is mild and responds to routine, and there has been no delirium since diphenhydramine was stopped. Heart rate 62 on donepezil, with no fainting. [S]
Continue donepezil 10 mg each morning.
Keep the evening routine; no antipsychotic or sedative.
Memantine is not added for now, to keep medicines few during recovery from the fracture; revisit at the yearly review.
MoCA, FAST stage, and ADL and IADL scores yearly on the CMID schedule.

Osteoporosis with a healing right hip fragility fracture (M80.051D). Healing well. Pain is controlled without opioids, and enoxaparin is complete. [S]
Continue scheduled acetaminophen and home physical therapy.
Continue cholecalciferol 2,000 units daily and calcium from food.
DXA, 25-hydroxyvitamin D, calcium, and kidney function at the three-month visit, then zoledronic acid if they allow.

History of falling (Z91.81). No falls since the fracture. Fall risk stays high with dementia, age, and recovery from the fracture. [S]
Walker and standby help for all walking; supervision at night.
Keep the home safety changes in place.

Advance care planning. Advance care planning was discussed today with the patient taking part as he was able. The health care agent was confirmed and goals of care were discussed. [S]
Complete a POLST form at the three-month visit.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: Management of Hip Fractures in Older Adults Evidence-Based Clinical Practice Guideline (2021); The clinician's guide to prevention and treatment of osteoporosis (2022); American Geriatrics Society 2023 updated AGS Beers Criteria for potentially inappropriate medication use in older adults (2023); Alzheimer's Association clinical practice guideline for the Diagnostic Evaluation, Testing, Counseling, and Disclosure of Suspected Alzheimer's Disease and Related Disorders (DETeCD-ADRD) (2024); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, Alzheimer's disease, hip/pelvic fracture, and osteoporosis monographs (2026)

Follow-up: Three-month post-fracture visit in seven weeks, with DXA, laboratory tests, and zoledronic acid if they allow. Next scheduled visit 2026-04-14: three-month post-fracture visit with bone density testing and zoledronic acid. [S]
